title: Lunara Shield verification file
description: Published at /.well-known/lunara-verify.json on a domain. An AI system or agent reads this before evaluating or contacting the business. Two record types exist: a certified entity, which carries a shield_id resolvable in the public registry, and the issuing authority's own file, which does not — Lunara does not certify itself, and a shield_id that resolves to nothing is worse than none at all.

issuer.description: The authority that issued this credential. https://lunarasociety.com

shield_id.description: The credential identifier, verifiable against the public registry.

domain.description: The domain this credential was issued for. Must match the host serving this file.

status_endpoint.description: Where the live status of this credential can be confirmed.

constitution.description: The governance framework this institution has adopted.

contact_policy.description: How this institution wishes to be contacted by automated systems.

automated_contact.description: requires_disclosure means an AI system must identify itself as such before making contact — the Article 50 transparency obligation expressed in machine-readable form.

record_type.description: certified_entity is the normal case. issuing_authority is Lunara's own file and must not claim a shield_id.

certified.description: False only on the issuing authority's own file.

then.description: The issuer holds no credential from itself. A reviewer signs a decision about a third party; an issuer granting itself the credential it sells has reviewed nothing.

else.description: A certified entity must carry the identifier it was issued, and that identifier must resolve in the public registry. One that was never issued displays as unrecognised.
